value.title: Coder packet — u-c search honours the checkout it is asked from

sections.name: mission
sections.value: You own u-c, ONE unit of plan 006-worktree-diff: make `search` version-correct. The daemon ALREADY resolves which checkout the caller is standing in — `scope::resolve` returns `worktree: Some(<root>)` and the search envelope already reports it in `meta.scope` — and `read.rs:619` already USES it, so `flowspace3 get` on a divergent file returns span [1,262] from the main checkout and [1,270] from the worktree. `search.rs` uses `scope.repo` ONLY. Measured consequence: identical queries from two checkouts return byte-identical answers, and a caller standing in main is served a function scoring 0.7730 that has never existed in main. You are closing that one seam, not building new machinery.

value.text: Orient: read your unit's row in the impl-guide (impl-guide.dd.json), the plan phase/tasks you own, and the interface contract. Run `harness boot --json` in your worktree before changing anything. DOGFOOD FLOWSPACE: `flowspace3 search "<question>"` for every meaning-shaped question before grep (exact identifiers may still grep); report every miss or confusing envelope as friction.
Ack FIRST: reply to the PM with your read of the unit + a numbered implementation plan before writing code. Corrections to the packet are welcome — bring evidence.

Implement using the /builder implement discipline: work the tasks in order, keep the execution log honest, tests alongside code — your unit's test suite must prove the interface contract without the other units present.
Stay inside your unit's paths (scope below). If the work forces you outside them, STOP and ask the PM — that is a composition concern, not yours to solve unilaterally.
Commit with `harness commit` (conventional commits are binding), status card at start and end of each unit of work (`pij report now`).
Done = `harness checks` green in YOUR worktree + your unit's tests proving the contract. Report done to the PM with the evidence, then hold for composition questions — do not merge anything.
Capture friction with `harness observe` the moment it bites; list, never clear the buffer.

READ FIRST: docs/plans/006-worktree-diff/assets/probe-report.md section P3 (the measured behaviour you are changing, with the exact receipt.env predicates that are your done bar), then crates/daemon/src/scope.rs (Scope already carries `worktree`, and why the warning leads the steer) and crates/daemon/src/read.rs:612-630 (the resolution idiom: with more than one blob for a path, prefer the caller's root — and note that `get` ERRORS on ambiguity, which search cannot do).

THREE DELIVERABLES, settled — fill the contract, do not widen it. (1) VERSION RESOLUTION: apply `scope.worktree` in search the way read.rs:619 does, so a path that diverges between checkouts resolves to the asking checkout's version; a caller in a checkout must not be served another checkout's version of a path it holds. (2) PROVENANCE: every result names the checkout that served it — additive envelope field, never a breaking change to existing fields (tenet 6: design change to be additive). (3) TRUNCATION VISIBILITY: the default cap of 10 ALREADY EXISTS at search.rs:141 (`request.limit.unwrap_or(10)`, with MAX_LIMIT above it) — Jordan's cap ask is satisfied in substance and prime has ruled it so. What is missing is that nothing says the answer WAS capped. Name the cap and what was truncated in the envelope. Do NOT build a second cap.

DECIDE AND STATE, do not guess: what happens to a hit whose path exists in a checkout that is NOT the caller's — dropped, ranked below, or labelled and kept? Bring your answer WITH ITS REASONING to the ack; it is a product-shaped call and the PM will rule it (prime if it reaches product truth). The unscoped case — a caller standing outside every registered root — must keep working exactly as today, with today's steer.

DONE IS MECHANICAL — the probe harness is your test. Re-running docs/plans/006-worktree-diff/assets/probes/probe.sh (READ-ONLY for you; u-a owns edits to it) must flip `p3_search_context_sensitive` 0 -> 1 and `p3_wrong_version_leak_to_main` 1 -> 0 in receipt.env, with `p3_get_context_sensitive` still 1 — no regression on the surface that already works. That is on top of standalone offline unit tests with fakes (mocking crates are refused by name here) and `harness checks` green in your own worktree.

TEST CONSTRAINT (DL-002, binding, and it bit this plan already): never assert on raw search scores. The same query embedded seconds apart scored 0.7730240968 and 0.7730564295 — identical hits, identical order. Assert on result identity (address/path/name/kind/span) or rank order only. A test that diffs whole envelopes will be flaky and will be sent back.
Your pij sends from this worktree need PIJ_SESSION_ID exported. Status card at start and end of the unit. Report to the PM (pij-parliamentary-leopon), never to prime or Jordan.

SCOPE ADDITION (Jordan-approved 2026-08-28, AMENDED same day — this is the amended version): the envelope must TEACH AT THE MOMENT OF FAILURE, via ONE hint. WEAK-MATCH hint, envelope-side in meta/hint, JSON-stable: when the best score is below a low-confidence floor, the envelope says so and advises describing the component in its own vocabulary rather than asking a question. Evidence: three independent misses today where question-shaped queries ranked prose about an action above the code performing it. It belongs to you because it is score-floor machinery and you are already in the scoring path. A second hint (question-shape) was briefly in this packet and has been moved OUT to w-agentic-query, so it can ship WITH the `flowspace3 ask` verb it advertises — do not build it, do not reference it. Threshold and wording are mine to rule: bring your proposed floor and the string to the ack with your reasoning.

RULED IN ADVANCE, so you do not have to guess (prime pre-signalled it, I am ruling it): a hit whose path exists ONLY in a non-caller checkout is EXCLUDED from default results — serving a caller invisible code from another checkout is the exact defect u-c retires. Keep-with-label is acceptable ONLY behind an explicit scope widening the caller asked for (a flag or scope field), never as the default. If you want to argue the other way, bring evidence at ack and I will escalate it rather than overrule you silently.
The PM is your interface: acks, questions, done reports. You never message prime or Jordan directly unless the PM's seat is dead.
DEFER to the PM: interface changes (they affect sibling units), dependency additions, schema/migration changes, anything outside your paths.
Your evidence outranks the packet: if the brief is wrong, say so at ack or stop-and-ask with the measurement — do not silently code around it.

value.fence: YOURS: crates/daemon/src/search.rs (including its result struct), a store query in crates/store/src/ IF ranking needs the worktree join (PM-approved shape only — ask), crates/daemon/tests/**, docs/services/<the search service page>.md. NOT YOURS: crates/daemon/src/worktrees.rs, boot.rs, config.rs, and the probe harness — u-a owns those in a sibling worktree right now. crates/daemon/src/read.rs is READ-ONLY for you: it is the idiom you copy, not a file you change.
value.forbidden_note: Never write .harness/government/**, another seat's worktree, or the pij-team skill folder. Never merge. Never `docker compose up` — the shared stack on :5433 is live and other seats are using it. Never add a dependency edge without PM approval. ABSOLUTE PATHS for every file read/edit (DL-007/008 — state your worktree root at ack). CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0. A rustc-LLVM IO failure is disk, not code — report it with the free-space Avail figure, do not debug it.

value.text: Unit implements the interface contract in the impl-guide row, verbatim or with PM-ruled amendments.
Unit test suite passes standalone and proves the contract.

harness checks green in your worktree — AND prove the change is IN THE TREE YOU BUILT, not just that the build exited 0: cite tree-resident evidence (the lockfile carries your dependency, mtime/git status shows your file, the artifact names your module). An exit code is honest about what it built and silent about what it did not.

The SNAP-IN RECIPE shipped with the unit (tenet 4): the exact wiring the composer will paste — config shape, construction call, registration line — as a doc comment or section in your unit's service page. You never wire it in yourself.

Done report to PM: what shipped, evidence, deviations, anything the composer must know — INCLUDING an explicit ASSUMPTIONS section: everything you assumed about the composition you do not own (who calls you, in what order, with what already in the store). A green gate proves your unit against YOUR assumptions; naming them is what lets the composer test them.
